finding: ClayVMArtifact/v1 self-describes vm_blob_sha256, while ProvenanceExpectation currently binds source/grammar/executable-IR identities only. General strict ClayOS callers therefore do not independently bind the expected VM core identity at admission. ClayEnvManifest/v1 already mitigates artifact substitution by checking trusted artifact_sha256 before launch and records vm_blob_sha256, but the reusable admission API should consume that VM identity directly rather than only post-check it.
candidate_change: Reject artifact header VM identity that differs from the caller-supplied expected VM identity before load_module/process admission.
Make clayenv run pass manifest.vm_blob_sha256 into ProvenanceExpectation.
Retain artifact payload SHA and whole-artifact SHA checks as independent integrity layers.
strong_ordinary_falsifier: Construct a different valid CLAYVM/1 core returning 666, keep original source/grammar/executable-IR identities, recompute the artifact header vm_blob_sha256 so the artifact is internally self-consistent, and require VM_BLOB_IDENTITY_MISMATCH against the trusted original expectation before process admission.
